name: CAPTURE and capture boundaries
desc: Covers CAPTURE and the observable boundaries of SEQMIN/SEQMAX: false versus empty successful results, exact/partial matching, group length preferences before start preferences, substructure placement, unnamed groups, empty spans, capture names, paths, namespaces, failure isolation, and integration with CAP and SLICE. Includes an independently enumerated 80-case split matrix.

tests.name: Group boundaries and preferences
tests.desc: Group preferences are resolved only among complete successful matches. Compare all preferred lengths in specification order before any preferred starts. Unnamed groups keep their preference, and inner-array preferences do not rank parent placements.

tests.name: Partial captures prefer shortest groups independently of total consumption
Capture preferences resolve after the entire exact match
Earlier group length preferences take priority
Unnamed groups retain their length preference
Equal capture lengths prefer the earliest start
Partial captures can select a later endpoint
Common expressions expose root named sequences
Substructure captures select earliest placements in specification order
Empty unnamed groups do not create a capture
Root substructure placement is independent of frontier order
Later group length preference outranks an earlier group start
Earlier group start takes priority over a later group start
Mixed preferences resolve in specification order
Unnamed shortest groups retain their preference
Inner capture length does not favor a later parent substructure
Root length preference outranks earliest substructure placement
Successful unnamed captures return an empty object
Successful empty matching returns an object rather than false
A named empty sequence produces a zero-length capture
An empty sequence cannot satisfy nonempty exact input
Numeric named-sequence opcodes retain their preferences
Computed names and uniqueness
tests.desc: Names are evaluated with NODE missing but lexical TEMP intact. Duplicate names are invalid across the entire observable match, including nested arrays and integer/string collisions.

tests.name: Capture names evaluate with NODE missing
Capture names retain lexical TEMP bindings
Duplicate names in one array reject the capture
Integer and string capture names collide after coercion
Capture names must be unique across nested arrays
Named-group syntax
tests.desc: CAPTURE requires exactly one argument. Named sequences require a name and may appear only at the root of a specification applied to array elements.

tests.name: SEQMAX cannot be nested in active sequence context
SEQMIN cannot be nested in active sequence context
Exhaustive split matrix
tests.desc: Enumerates every legal split for lengths 0 through 4, all eight MIN/MAX assignments to three groups, and partial/exact matching. Expected results rank all group lengths before any group starts, independently of successor traversal.

tests.name: Capture names
tests.desc: Empty strings and integers are valid names; integers become strings. Names that shadow host methods, including __proto__ where supported, are ordinary output properties.

tests.name: Capture key  is an own data property
Capture key 0 is an own data property
Capture key -1 is an own data property
Capture key constructor is an own data property
Capture key toString is an own data property
Capture key hasOwnProperty is an own data property
Capture key __proto__ is an own data property
Runtime name failures
tests.desc: Computed boolean, fractional, object, and array names are invalid operands. CAPTURE traps those match failures and returns false without exposing partial captures.

tests.name: Invalid runtime name false rejects CAPTURE
Invalid runtime name true rejects CAPTURE
Outer capture isolation
tests.desc: A CAPTURE call starts an independent match state. It may reuse an outer name, and neither successful nor partially failed inner matching changes the enclosing CAP namespace.

tests.name: An independent CAPTURE may reuse an outer name without changing CAP
Failed CAPTURE leaves the outer namespace intact
Paths under AT
tests.desc: AT changes the match root. Capture paths exclude the outer prefix and can be passed directly to SLICE while that current node is retained.

tests.name: AT prefixes are excluded and captured ranges still work with SLICE
Success, failure, and alternate targets
tests.desc: CAPTURE returns false for a failed match and an object for every successful match, even when no groups are named. Its argument is match context. Alternate targets start a fresh matching root, and ordinary function results are compared as data.

tests.name: Paths and observable spans
tests.desc: Capture paths identify arrays relative to the match root. Offsets/counts/limits refer to array elements, not the sizes of string elements. Nested properties with arbitrary names remain path elements. CAPTURE does not install its returned object into CAP.

tests.name: String values are single array elements
Returned data independence
tests.desc: Capture results and their path arrays are ordinary mutable data. Modifying one result must not change a second result or an enclosing CAP namespace.

tests.name: Returned path does not alias CAP
Fatal errors
tests.desc: CAPTURE converts ordinary match failure to false but must not swallow malformed expressions or resource exhaustion. Name failures remain recoverable match failures as tested above.
